publicReleaseNotes: Lamp 1.10.0 starts your status page from your website, sets itself up, connects PagerDuty and turns bare https:// URLs in updates into links. First run asks for your website, reads it once and fills in the page name, tagline, mark, accent color and first components, every fact editable; a site Lamp cannot read leaves plain defaults. The setup checklist is gone: Lamp checks its own public page and subscribe form after every publish and every minute, and Overview shows one line. Alerts can connect PagerDuty: signed v3 events create private drafts and brief entries, and an optional sealed REST API key posts each publication back as a note; the key never leaves in a backup. A bare https:// URL in an update becomes a link on the page, in feeds and in email (tracking off), <url> in Slack and a link in Teams; a webhook subscriber that registered a Slack incoming-webhook URL gets Slack's message form, and every other webhook subscriber keeps Lamp's format byte for byte. A local backup from any earlier Lamp, including one made before 1.8.0, restores with rer import, also into a database Run Edit Run Managed installed, and rer export --target remote backs up the hosted installation. Run Edit Run Business can check a move's cutover status, and the status page host answers /health. It pins rer 0.2.76 with no local patch. Two additive migrations, 0041 and 0042, apply on update; no configuration changes; back up first and run rer deploy as before. PAGE-004.summary: Overall status: spelling only, meaning unchanged.

PAGE-006.summary: Serving through a failure: spelling only, meaning unchanged.
PAGE-006.was: Serving through a failure: When the database, the queue, or object storage is unreachable, the three surfaces in PAGE-005 return 200 — from the current snapshot, or from the cached response under the `stale-if-error` directive of PAGE-007 when the origin itself cannot answer. They return 503 only when no snapshot has ever been written. A response that could not be built from current data states the instant its content was generated and is labelled as the last known state; no failed read ever produces the all-clear of PAGE-004. `/health` still reports 503 per BASE-OPS-001; the public page's availability does not depend on it.

They return 503 only when no snapshot has ever been written. PAGE-007.summary: Publish latency and caching: spelling only, meaning unchanged.
PAGE-007.was: Publish latency and caching: Stable public URLs validate the current snapshot generation on reuse with a generation ETag and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, stale-if-error=3600`. Immutable artifact bytes are cached by generation and artifact key; advancing the published generation makes previous cache entries ineligible for a healthy current response. An update, component state change, or maintenance transition is readable on the status page, history, incident and maintenance permalinks, Atom feed, widget and public JSON within 10 seconds of the request that caused it returning 200. An unreachable origin may use its retained response for the one-hour error window; the application also retains labelled last-known snapshots under PAGE-006.

PAGE-010.summary: Atom feed: spelling only, meaning unchanged.
PAGE-010.was: Atom feed: `/feed.atom` validates as Atom 1.0 and contains one entry for every published incident update and for every maintenance notice — scheduled, rescheduled, started, completed, cancelled — from the last 12 months, ordered newest first. An entry's identifier is stable from first publication and is never reused.

An entry's identifier is stable from first publication and is never reused.

PAGE-012.was: Branding: Page name, logo, accent colour, timezone, hostname, and a footer-credit toggle are set in settings without a code change. The footer credit is the plain static text `Powered by Lamp`, defaults on, and disabling it makes no network action. The logo is served from the deployment's own origin. The favicon composites a mark for the current overall status over the configured logo rather than replacing it, and the page carries Open Graph metadata whose title and image state the current overall status.

UPTIME-006.summary: Daily record: spelling only, meaning unchanged.
UPTIME-006.was: Daily record: The page shows one mark per day of the reporting window for each visible component. A day containing any downtime minute is labelled with the number of downtime minutes in that day. A day before the component's earliest state history entry is rendered as having no data and is visually distinct from a day with no downtime.

A day containing any downtime minute is labeled with the number of downtime minutes in that day. UPDATE-001.summary: Template: a bare https:// URL in any field now becomes a link (UPDATE-013); nothing else is interpreted, and the clause text is unchanged.
UPDATE-001.was: Template: Publishing an update requires at least one attached component, an affected-audience statement of at most 250 characters, a customer-impact statement of at most 250 characters, and, for a lifecycle other than Resolved, a next-update time. A resolved update requires no next-update time and carries no next-update promise on any surface, including when an older stored resolved update retains a time. A what-still-works statement of at most 250 characters and a details statement of at most 500 characters are optional. Every field is plain text; no HTML or markdown is interpreted. A publish request that omits a required field, exceeds a length, or attaches no component returns 400 and changes nothing. The next-update time is a commitment to publish again by then; it is never presented as an estimate of when the incident will be resolved.

UPDATE-002.summary: One rendering: every surface renders the same links from the shared renderer (UPDATE-013); the clause text is unchanged.
UPDATE-002.was: One rendering: The public page, the Atom feed, the widget payload, and the notification email render an update from the same renderer. No surface omits a populated field of the update or shows a field the update does not carry.
UPDATE-002.now: One rendering: The public page, the Atom feed, the widget payload, and the notification email render an update from the same renderer. No surface omits a populated field of the update or shows a field the update does not carry. With UPDATE-013, each surface renders a bare https:// URL from that renderer: a link whose text is the URL on the page, feeds and email HTML part, and the bare URL in the email text part.

UPDATE-005.was: Drafts: An unpublished update appears on no public surface. A draft is saved within 2 seconds of the last edit and is restored unchanged after a browser reload. Publication consumes that draft and opens an empty draft for the next update, with lifecycle prompts. A stale tab cannot resurrect published wording or overwrite a newer acknowledged draft. Draft writes, template application, scheduling and publication require the acknowledged draft version. A fresh empty composer is not reported saved until a native write is acknowledged; Publish requires a complete acknowledged draft. Reconciliation after a lost acknowledgement identifies the attempted write and preserves later workflow changes.

MAINT-006.summary: Rescheduling and cancellation: spelling only, meaning unchanged.
MAINT-006.was: Rescheduling and cancellation: Changing the window of a scheduled maintenance notifies every subscriber already notified about it. Cancelling it publishes a cancellation notice to those same subscribers, removes it from the upcoming list within 10 seconds, and keeps it in the maintenance history marked cancelled.
MAINT-006.now: Rescheduling and cancellation: Changing the window of a scheduled maintenance notifies every subscriber already notified about it. Canceling it publishes a cancellation notice to those same subscribers, removes it from the upcoming list within 10 seconds, and keeps it in the maintenance history marked canceled.

SUB-009.summary: Webhook subscribers: an endpoint that is a Slack incoming-webhook URL receives Slack's message form, signed the same way, with each bare https:// URL as <url>, never <url|text>; every other endpoint receives Lamp's format with every update field byte for byte.
SUB-009.was: Webhook subscribers: An endpoint URL and a contact email address together subscribe as a webhook subscriber; the address exists so SUB-010 can say why the endpoint was deactivated. Each notification is a POST carrying `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` headers, where the signature is a space-separated list of versioned HMAC-SHA256 values over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`, so a secret can be rotated without a gap. The body carries the incident, every update it has published, and each attached component's previous and new state, so a receiver that missed a delivery needs no prior state. It carries no subscriber address. A delivery succeeds only on a 2xx within 30 seconds; a redirect is a failure. A Slack incoming-webhook URL receives the same events with a Slack-formatted body.
SUB-009.now: Webhook subscribers: An endpoint URL and a contact email address together subscribe as a webhook subscriber; the address exists so SUB-010 can say why the endpoint was deactivated. Each notification is a POST carrying `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, and `webhook-signature` headers, where the signature is a space-separated list of versioned HMAC-SHA256 values over `{webhook-id}.{webhook-timestamp}.{raw body}`, so a secret can be rotated without a gap. The body carries the incident, every update it has published, and each attached component's previous and new state, so a receiver that missed a delivery needs no prior state. It carries no subscriber address. A delivery succeeds only on a 2xx within 30 seconds; a redirect is a failure. An endpoint that is a Slack incoming-webhook URL (host `hooks.slack.com`) receives the same events, signed the same way, as Slack's message form: its text carries each bare `https://` URL from an update field as `<url>`, never `<url|text>`, and its rich-text link elements show the URL itself, so every field reassembles unchanged (UPDATE-013). Every other endpoint receives Lamp's format, whose update fields are the published text byte for byte.

SETUP-001.summary: Setup readiness: setup asks the owner nothing Lamp can do itself; Lamp checks its own page, subscribe form and sender, and Overview shows one live line instead of an eight-step checklist (owner decision, 20 October 2026).
SETUP-001.was: Setup readiness: Overview shows eight steps from saved server state: non-sample page name and branding, configured time zone, sender checked, first component, first published incident, public page opened through its protected check, reachable subscription form, and public address selected with custom-domain documentation. Open steps lead to their completion screen; all-complete collapses the checklist. Local development suppresses outgoing mail, offers no captured-mail inbox, and prepares automatic one-click owner entry without email (owner decision, 15 October 2026). To prove a subscriber notice was produced locally, publish to an active subscriber, let dispatch run, and inspect its `suppressed` outcome in Notifications or `GET /api/app/deliveries`; `notification_deliveries` records that outcome without a provider-acceptance claim. The local sender check explicitly reports suppression and requires a hosted installation to check provider authentication; that hosted check does not claim inbox delivery. Public GET paths remain database-free; protected operator actions retain the public-read checks. Choosing an address acknowledges that choice, not DNS validation, and the default deployment address is supported.
SETUP-001.now: Setup readiness: Setup asks the owner nothing that Lamp can do itself (owner decision, 20 October 2026). Every change republishes the public page, and Lamp checks its own public page and subscribe form after each publish and on the minute Cron, reading the real rendered form, and checks a hosted sender with the mail provider when it changes and daily. Overview shows one line: the page is live at its address, when it was published and when the page and form were checked, with Review page (Your page, `/app/page`: Lamp's preview of the page, what it checked and ways to try it) and Change address (Settings). A failing check turns that line amber with a short reason and the one thing to do. Results belong to the address they were read from. The deployment address is the public address by default; a custom domain is optional. Local development suppresses outgoing mail, offers no captured-mail inbox, and prepares automatic one-click owner entry without email (owner decision, 15 October 2026). To prove a subscriber notice was produced locally, publish to an active subscriber, let dispatch run, and inspect its `suppressed` outcome in Notifications or `GET /api/app/deliveries`; `notification_deliveries` records that outcome without a provider-acceptance claim. Locally the sender is reported as email being off, never as verified; the hosted check reads provider authentication and does not claim inbox delivery. Public GET paths remain database-free.

SETUP-002.summary: First-run setup: asks for the owner's website first and fills in what the site gives, every fact editable (owner decision, 20 October 2026); spelling to US.
SETUP-002.was: First-run setup: A signed-in owner whose installation has no stored first-run completion is sent from every operator document to `/setup`, where they confirm the page name, tagline, time zone and accent colour. Saving stores completion durably; afterwards `/setup` opens the app and settings remain editable in Settings. A signed-out visitor to `/setup` is sent to sign-in and returned there. An installation that already had an operator before this clause is recorded as complete by its migration. A setup rerun never clears completion.
SETUP-002.now: First-run setup: A signed-in owner whose installation has no stored first-run completion is sent from every operator document to `/setup`, which asks for their website first (owner decision, 20 October 2026). Lamp reads that public site once, refusing private and loopback addresses on every hop and running none of its scripts, and fills in what the site gives: page name, tagline, mark (stored as a PNG), accent colour and components from its navigation, plus the time zone from the browser; it never invents what the site did not give. A site that cannot be read, or no website, leaves plain defaults with one calm line. Every fact stays editable before and after; confirming stores the settings, the mark and the components and stores completion durably; afterwards `/setup` opens the app and settings remain editable in Settings. A signed-out visitor to `/setup` is sent to sign-in and returned there. An installation that already had an operator before this clause is recorded as complete by its migration. A setup rerun never clears completion.

MOVE-006.summary: Cutover preview: spelling only, meaning unchanged.
MOVE-006.was: Cutover preview: Settings → Cutover is available after a dry run and for saved imports. It shows up to the first 25 old incident and maintenance addresses with proposed or surviving native permalinks, unavailable addresses and source-host limits, source feed answers, unsupported JSON/RSS/widget consumers, and eligible invitations with their original expiry deadline. Once the owner selects a public origin, each Opens check uses a credentialless browser request that follows the redirect and verifies the final native address and successful HTML response; failures remain explicit. The ordered guide covers import, preview, explicit invitations, hostname/custom-domain instructions, rechecking and keeping the source through the confirmation window. It claims neither DNS validation nor inbox delivery. Instatus accepts its documented saved management REST response families with a separate owner acknowledgement that the page and supplied history are published and unrestricted. Known protected or unpublished source records cannot become public. Visual Component parents are groups; audience groups are refused access restrictions. Only confirmed, approved email-only subscriptions with resolved preferences become pending. Exact supplied public-summary incident/maintenance URLs are joined by source ID; missing URLs are not invented. Maintenance ends use explicit timestamps or documented duration minutes under completed/autoEnd semantics, with every update retained silently. Sorry general notices may have no affected component and are carried as resolved informational history without outage claims; cancelled maintenance stays cancelled. Sorry additionally accepts keyless public JSON captures, including paginated components and notices plus full detail for every notice. Partial public previews name uncaptured details and cannot be applied. Subscribers come only from the authenticated API; eligible email rows are held inert without mail or confirmation expiry. A held row neither released nor undone is deleted with its address 30 days after the reviewed dry run, and Cutover states that date. After the hostname is live and the watch window closes, an explicit owner invitation action names the configured public origin, records that approval, and releases held rows into pending with a 72-hour window starting at release. Undo cannot recall mail or remove a released row as if it were still unchanged. Sorry numeric notice IDs and supplied notice paths redirect to surviving Lamp incidents or maintenance; `/notices`, `/history` and `/history/YYYY/month` (English month names) redirect to Lamp’s `/history/` while a Sorry import is retained.

migrations.buyerSteps: Apply after 0040. Adds the Business import door's archive tables (ik_door_archives, ik_door_archive_chunks) for the door's archive and restore-check actions. Additive; no existing row changes.

Apply after 0041. Adds PagerDuty's responder columns to alert_sources (responder_preset, responder_sealed_credentials, responder_connected) and the alert_responder_posts table for publication notes (INTAKE-009). Additive; existing sources, mappings and receipts are unchanged.

agentUpdateInstructions: Back up data and owner source first: node scripts/export.mjs --remote with the deployment's --env-file (or rer export --target remote --output DIR with the Cloudflare credentials exported), plus Settings → Export page data. Update the checkout to v1.10.0 and run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; the checkout pins rer 0.2.76 and carries no rer patch. If your fork adapted the import door (modules/import-kit/src/door), take Base's door at rer-v0.2.71 and re-apply only owner changes; if it changed Lamp's archive policy, carry that change into scripts/installer/archive-policy.mjs, which scripts/installer/local.mjs now names as its policyModule. Then run rer deploy with the same environment and input file (add --owner-name when it asks without a terminal). Migrations 0041_import_door_archives.sql and 0042_responder_sources.sql apply on deploy, in order (additive: the Business import door's archive tables, then PagerDuty's responder columns and note records); no input changes. On Run Edit Run Managed hosting, back up and restore with node scripts/export.mjs and node scripts/import.mjs as OPERATIONS.md describes; a local rer export backup also restores into a new Managed installation with rer import. Run rer verify and pnpm run validate:release before adopting.
